exposure: low-risk women (term delivery and no pregnancy or medical complications)
Hispanic women (Mexican, Hispanic Caribbean, Central/South American)
cohort: 961,381 women giving birth in New York City from 1995 to 2003
finding: After adjusting for multiple risk factors, Hispanic Caribbean and African American women had the highest risk of cesarean delivery compared to non-Hispanic white women, and immigrant status further increased the risk within Hispanic subgroups.
